text: 44-year-old female. The patient presents to the emergency department with confusion that started this morning. The patient's husband reports that she initially complained of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and fatigue after eating and has vomited 3 times. The patient has progressively become more confused throughout the day. The patient's past medical history includes morbid obesity, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, a sleeve gastrectomy 1 month ago, and depression with multiple suicide attempts.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Factitious disorder (Munchausen syndrome) by proxy or self-induced insulin abuse, leading to severe hypoglycemia and subsequent confusion and vomiting. The clinical picture of a post-bariatric surgery patient with profound hypoglycemia (41 mg/dL), normal C-peptide, and a history of psychiatric instability and suicide attempts strongly suggests exogenous insulin administration. I am requesting an insulin antibody level and a detailed review of the patient's medication supply.
